title: Gains arising from changes in fair value of biological assets less NON-CURRENT ASSETS
columns:
Comments on the results
The year 2008-09 has seen an improvement in the financial performance of the Group. The Group’s overall turnover increased by 49% from Kshs 1.46 billion in the 2007/08 to Kshs 2.18 billion in 2008/09. In terms of profit, the Group posted a profit aftertax arising from
operating activities of Kshs. 137.2 million compared to a loss of Kshs. 13.4 million, recorded in the previous year.
The increase in revenue was due to stronger international tea prices and also an increase in total tea and coffee production andsales compared to the previous year. The results were, however, adversely affected by the strengthening of the Kenya shillingduring the second half
of the year and the continuing rise in costs of inputs particularly in relation to energy, labour and farm inputs.
The total assets of the Group increased to Kshs. 8 billion due to the revaluation carried out during the year.
Despite the effects of the drought, Sasini managed to increase its overall production in both tea and coffee. The effects ofthe drought were more severe in the coffee sector and despite increased production, there was a drop in quality that affected the proportion of premium
grade coffee and as a consequence of which there was a decline in the prices realized per kilogram. The tea sector experienced improved price realization at the auctions, fuelled by under supply in the global tea markets. The volumes improved compared to the previous year,

The dairy and horticulture sectors were negatively affected by the drought but remained marginally profitable during the financial year.
The Group continued to implement its diversification strategy during the year with increased throughput in its coffee millingoperations and with an increase in the number of Savanna coffee lounges.
The Group’s diversification into value added activities continues to bear fruit with positive results from the new initiatives, namely, the Coffee Mill, Savanna Coffee Lounge, and the Export Operations. However, high tea prices continue to impact negatively on the performance of
value added retail products.
The Group has continued to service its bond interest obligations and the first redemption is due in June 2010.
Dividend
An interim dividend of 20% (Ksh0.20 per share) was paid to shareholders on 10th June 2009.
The Directors will recommend to the members at the forthcoming Annual General Meeting, the payment of a final dividend of 20%(Ksh0.20 per share) for the year ended 30thSeptember 2009, payable less withholding tax, where applicable on or about 4thMarch 2010 to the
members on the register at close of business on 18thFebruary 2010. The Company’s register will be closed for one day on 19thFebruary 2010.
Annual General Meeting
The 58thAnnual General Meeting of the members will be held at Kamundu Estate, Kiambu on Thursday, 25thFebruary 2010 at 11.30 am.
